bracket: [Textbook answer-key error in a name the key VOLUNTEERS — the structure it draws is correct, and the structure is all this question asks for. The key names the compound \(4\)-Ethylhex-3-ene. Numbering the six-carbon chain from either end puts the double bond at C-3, so that criterion ties and the tie is broken by giving the SUBSTITUENT the lower locant: the ethyl group is C-3 from one end and C-4 from the other, so the preferred name is \(3\)-Ethylhex-3-ene. The book applies this same tiebreak correctly elsewhere in the chapter, at Problem 9.7(iv), which is what shows this to be a slip rather than a house convention.]

[Textbook answer-key errors, and the first is self-refuting on the key's own reaction scheme. In part (ii) the key's final product is DRAWN as 1-bromo-3-chlorobenzene — a bromine where the nitro group belongs. Its own preceding step nitrates benzene with conc. \(\text{HNO}_3\)/conc. \(\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4\) to give nitrobenzene, and no bromine-bearing reagent appears anywhere in the sequence, so the bromine cannot have come from the route the key itself draws; the product of that route is 1-chloro-3-nitrobenzene. Confirmed at 5x magnification on the printed page. Secondary, in part (iii): the key prescribes DILUTE \(\text{HNO}_3\) and DILUTE \(\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4\) for a ring nitration, where its own parts (i) and (ii) and the chapter's own text all use the CONCENTRATED acids. The answer below uses the concentrated reagents.]

[Textbook answer-key error, self-refuting on the equation's own atom balance. Part (c) is printed \(\text{C}_5\text{H}_{10}(g) + \tfrac{17}{2}\text{O}_2(g) \rightarrow 6\text{CO}_2(g) + 5\text{H}_2\text{O}(g)\), which cannot balance: five carbons on the left cannot give six \(\text{CO}_2\) on the right. Every other atom already balances for \(\text{C}_6\text{H}_{10}\) — hydrogen \(10 \rightarrow 5\text{H}_2\text{O}\), oxygen \(17 \rightarrow 12 + 5\) — so the formula is a misprint for hexyne, \(\text{C}_6\text{H}_{10}\), and the coefficients the key prints are the correct ones for it. The answer below uses \(\text{C}_6\text{H}_{10}\).]

[Textbook error in a drawn structure, affecting the picture rather than the answer. For part (a)(ii) the key draws \(\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_3\), in which the second carbon is shown carrying two hydrogens AND a double bond — five bonds to one carbon, which cannot exist. The NAME the key prints beside it, But-2-ene, is correct, and corresponds to \(\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_3\); one hydrogen has simply been left on the drawn structure. The answer below gives the tetravalent structure.]
